title: Raid on Sirhind and the Khalsa’s March to Amritsar

blocks.text: With Kapoor Singh’s approval, the Singhs move swiftly against Sirhind and strike before the city can organize an effective defense. The attack is presented as both vengeance and necessity, joining old grievance to the immediate need for supplies and mobility.

The raid is methodical rather than chaotic. The Khalsa occupied the five main entrances to the city, carries out a concentrated sack, gathers animals and valuables, and avoids becoming trapped in a prolonged engagement that would invite a stronger Mughal response.

After only a short stay, the Singhs regroup and begin moving again, now better provisioned for the road to Amritsar. Their success also deepens Khalsa influence in Malwa, where communities see both the Panth’s striking power and its willingness to answer local appeals.
